priorStories.headline: Houthis take Red Sea island; Saudi pipeline closes
priorStories.body:
Iran-backed Houthi forces captured Mayun, also known as Perim, after taking the nearby Yemeni port of Mokha the previous day. The island sits at the entrance to the Red Sea near a major shipping route.

Saudi Arabia separately shut its East-West oil pipeline as a precaution after drone attacks. The pipeline has provided an alternative export route while the Iran war disrupts shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

priorStories.headline: Philippine ferry fire death toll reaches 35
priorStories.body:
Rescuers recovered 30 bodies from the burned MV June Aster, bringing the confirmed toll from the September 9 passenger-ferry fire to at least 35.

Authorities reported 43 survivors among the 132 people aboard. More than 50 people remained missing.

priorStories.headline: Diesel tops $6 as monthly inflation quickens
priorStories.body:
U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in August from July, after a 0.1% monthly increase in July. Prices were 3.4% higher than a year earlier, unchanged from the previous annual reading.

The national average diesel price separately exceeded $6 a gallon, a nominal record, amid fuel-supply disruptions caused by the Iran war.

candidates.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi. The meeting was part of efforts by the two neighboring countries to improve relations strained by their deadly 2020 border clash.
candidates.title: Modi and Xi meet at BRICS summit

candidates.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season set a satellite-era record for the latest point in the year without a hurricane forming. The National Hurricane Center listed five named Atlantic storms but no hurricanes as of September 12, with accumulated cyclone energy 93% below the 1991–2020 norm.
candidates.title: Atlantic season sets record for latest first hurricane

candidates.summary: Saudi civil defense said a projectile fell in Al-Tawwal governorate near the Yemeni border late Saturday, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and several other buildings. Saudi authorities blamed the Houthis; the group had not immediately claimed responsibility.
candidates.title: Projectile injures two near Saudi-Yemen border
